dialogues.speaker: Leader
dialogues.text: Very well... You speak true. We must reconsider our actions. I... In truth, I do not know how things came to this...

dialogues.speaker: Leader
dialogues.text: There's been a strange feeling in my heart since this war broke out.

dialogues.speaker: Leader
dialogues.text: We were meant to pursue freedom and happiness, but Phobos led us here instead, step by step...

dialogues.speaker: Leader
dialogues.text: Has something gone wrong? What could it be?

dialogues.speaker: Leader
dialogues.text: If you meet with the Sebastos upon your return, please apprise him of our circumstances and our doubts.

dialogues.speaker: Leader
dialogues.text: You'll be doing us a truly great favor.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't worry, we will!

dialogues.speaker: Este
dialogues.text: It seems that you've resolved our previous problem.

dialogues.speaker: Este
dialogues.text: I suppose that means you'll be rushing ahead toward your next goal, then?

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: Yes. I'll be counting on you to take care of this place, Este...

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: Also, remember that it is better to trust the wisdom of your heart rather than handing all judgment of right and wrong over to Phobos or any Harmost.

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: The Sebastos created Phobos to free us from our servitude to destiny, but the people's blind faith has led us into enslavement more frightful still.

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: In the future, you may encounter a similar choice once more. I hope you will make the right decision when the time comes.

dialogues.speaker: Este
dialogues.text: Dominus Cassiodor, why are you suddenly speaking of such things?

dialogues.speaker: Este
dialogues.text: Still, I shall keep your words in my heart. I, Este, shall uphold my own sense of justice.

dialogues.speaker: Osse
dialogues.text: That is good. Farewell, Este. I believe we shall meet again.

dialogues.speaker: Leader
dialogues.text: Hey, you! Yes, you! You gibbering imbecile! Why do you delay!? Even if we waste away, the treasure won't move itself, surely!

dialogues.speaker: The Dude They Call "Idiot"
dialogues.text: Nay, sir! It's just that they are simply too heavy! We've been at this all day, yet there's still so much left...

dialogues.speaker: Leader
dialogues.text: Where, then, is the intrinsic merit in feeding that prodigious size of yours!? It's treasure, you brute, treasure! Of course it's heavy!

dialogues.speaker: Leader
dialogues.text: Besides, we "confiscated" all these treasures from those accursed barbarians, did we not?

dialogues.speaker: Leader
dialogues.text: Leaving such wealth in the hands of those insects who live like swine and mongrels would be a terrible waste!

dialogues.speaker: The Dude They Call "Idiot"
dialogues.text: But Sir, don't you think we should've brought a few more ships if we wanted to haul all this back to Remuria?

dialogues.speaker: Leader
dialogues.text: What are you, slow? Imperial cargo ships are not to be used for such a thing!

dialogues.speaker: The Dude They Call "Idiot"
dialogues.text: Well, why don't we destroy what we cannot carry? Better than having it fall into the hands of these savages!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, is it just Paimon, or have we heard this conversation before...?

choices.text: Sounds like when we first arrived in Petrichor...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, those unlucky adventurers we drove off before were saying similar stuff.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Feels like this round's worse than the last, too!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is it possible they were turned into golems after the boat they were on sank?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's so creepy!

response.speaker: Este
response.text: Are you of Legio IX? What are you doing here? Should you all not have been ordered to retreat to Fort Charybdis?

response.speaker: Leader
response.text: Hey, Este! Don't you dare ruin our fun, you hear?

response.speaker: Leader
response.text: These barbarians are less of a threat than dead fish anyway, so just let us have our fun messing about here for a while longer, would you?

response.speaker: Este
response.text: These treasures... *sigh* I don't know what orders your Harmost gave you...

response.speaker: Este
response.text: But did the Sebastos not order us to subdue these ignorant tribes and free them of fate's shackles? Those orders do not include such... clearly criminal deeds.

response.speaker: Leader
response.text: Hah? Surely you jest! The orders of our commander, mighty Dominus Boethius, were indeed to punish these savages harshly.

response.speaker: Leader
response.text: And besides, we have received no punishment. That means that both Phobos and the Sebastos, our Imperator, approve of our actions.

response.speaker: Leader
response.text: So what's all this talk about crimes... Are you trying to start trouble?

response.speaker: Este
response.text: But...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There's another Este here? Well, aren't things getting weirder by the moment?

response.speaker: Osse
response.text: It appears that it is time to answer that question of yours.

response.speaker: Osse
response.text: The Este you met in town must be a descendant of Remurians. His ancestor must have followed me to join the new nation all those years ago, becoming an ordinary Fontainian.

response.speaker: Osse
response.text: As such, the "symphony" that has stolen these Fontainians' souls would not affect him. But in turn, the melody that records his ancestor's memories had nowhere to go, and so attached itself to that statue.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you mean that the Este here is Town-Este's ancestor, the real "Este the Quick-Witted"? What about the others?

response.speaker: Osse
response.text: Just wandering souls, lost in their memories. Let us go have a look.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You walk up together with Monsieur Os...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hello there, Este.

response.speaker: Este
response.text: Yes, hello. And who are you, exactly?

response.speaker: Este
response.text: You do not appear to be Remurians. Are you savages, then?

response.speaker: Este
response.text: Well, this is a battlefield, and you put yourselves in great peril. You should leave this place, regardless of who you are.

response.speaker: Osse
response.text: Este, it is I. It has been a while.

response.speaker: Este
response.text: ...Skies above, it's you, Dominus Cassiodor! You so rarely appear in this form that I almost failed to recognize you.

response.speaker: Este
response.text: And as for these two... Are they your attendants?

choices.text: You can just take that to be so.

response.speaker: Este
response.text: Still, Dominus Cassiodor, what brings you here? Did the Sebastos not send you to... Damnation! I cannot remember! Am I in some dream?

response.speaker: Osse
response.text: That does seem to be the case.

response.speaker: Este
response.text: Haha! Surely you jest! The Sebastos must have assigned you some secret mission again, or else I am an ignoramus!

response.speaker: Osse
response.text: You guess correctly. Speaking of which, why are the legionnaires of Legio IX guarding those chains?

response.speaker: Este
response.text: The chains... You mean the treasure, yes? I believe them to be spoils of war.

response.speaker: Este
response.text: Though the Sebastos views war as naught but a sad necessity in fulfilling our grand aspirations and has long outlawed such brutal behaviors...

response.speaker: Este
response.text: You know as well as I that they have become commonplace nonetheless... We are on the path of darkness, though none perceive it.

response.speaker: Este
response.text: Dominus Cassiodor, what has happened? Phobos was meant to bring us happiness, but all I feel is a pain I cannot name...

response.speaker: Osse
response.text: I, too, am searching for the answer to that question. But it appears that we will have to deal with the problem at hand first.

response.speaker: Este
response.text: Indeed. Still, those are our legionnaires, so let us solve things peacefully, if we may.

response.speaker: Este
response.text: ...Huh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hey, hey, {NICKNAME}, stop complicating things further! Don't worry, {M#he}{F#she} was just joking, Este, so please, continue.

choices.text: Oh, I can get pretty savage.
It's that bit with the "Treasure Hoarders" all over again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahem, legionnaires of Legio IX!

dialogues.speaker: Leader
dialogues.text: Huh? Who are you? Este's little helpers?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We're no ordinary helpers! Mighty are we who have come with Dominus Cassiodor, to attend and aid him.

response.speaker: Osse
response.text: (It seems you two have quite the penchant for acting.)

response.speaker: Leader
response.text: Dominus Cassiodor, you say... I heard that the Sebastos had sent him to Aremorica. Has he returned so soon?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, the one next to us is, in fact...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wh—Whatever the case, we have come to survey the frontline legions!

response.speaker: Leader
response.text: Right. I figured as much.

response.speaker: Leader
response.text: I mean, we haven't gone to Fort Charybdis with the main body of troops...

response.speaker: Leader
response.text: But we are the rearguard, so some final "cleanup" is well within our range of duties, eh?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Is this also a command from Phobos?

response.speaker: Leader
response.text: Well... It should have guided our every move, but since coming here, there have been many times when we could not hear its melody.

response.speaker: Leader
response.text: As such, we've fallen back on Dominus Boethius's directives.

response.speaker: Leader
response.text: Who do you think you are!? How dare you impugn Dominus Boethius's name so flagrantly!

response.speaker: Leader
response.text: A Harmost as esteemed as he follows the directives of the Sebastos in all things. His word is as the word of Phobos itself.

choices.text: Phobos could have made a mistake as well.

response.speaker: Leader
response.text: Hah! Are you sure you're Remurian? Do you not know that Phobos was fashioned by the omnipotent Sebastos and the infallible oracle?

choices.text: Yet you are not receiving the melody.

response.speaker: Leader
response.text: Well, that is true enough. But in what can we place our trust, if not Phobos?

response.speaker: Leader
response.text: Surely it would not stand idly by, were we to diverge from the correct path?

choices.text: The Sebastos does not permit the harm of innocent people.

response.speaker: Leader
response.text: Innocent, you say... Yes, he did task us with helping these vulnerable humans before the war began.

response.speaker: Leader
response.text: But our actions have the tacit approval of Phobos. Could its decrees ever be in conflict with the sacred word of the Sebastos?

choices.text: Phobos could have made a mistake as well.
Yet you are not receiving the melody.
We are special envoys of the Imperator, our Sebastos.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What kinda rank is that... Well, that's not completely wrong. We're with Dominus Cassiodor.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! Dominus Cassiodor's retainers, that's who we are!

dialogues.speaker: Leader
dialogues.text: You... Come to think of it, you could be barbarians in disguise, attempting to deceive us! You are, aren't you!?

dialogues.speaker: Leader
dialogues.text: You damnable worms, I shall slay you where you stand!

dialogues.speaker: Este
dialogues.text: Those are still our legionnaires, so let us try to resolve this peacefully, if we may.

dialogues.speaker: Este
dialogues.text: God King Above, thank you, Dominus Cassiodor. In any event, it seems that this issue has been resolved for now.

dialogues.speaker: Leader
dialogues.text: Phobos is a perfect creation. I counsel you, as a Remurian, to not doubt its directives.

response.speaker: Leader
response.text: What are we doing now, debating sophistry? Take it up with those musical erudites in the capital. A soldier's duty is to obey. Complex matters are not my strong suit...

response.speaker: Leader
response.text: Yes... That is possible. How did I not consider that? Could our rash actions have caused Phobos to cease guiding us?

response.speaker: Leader
response.text: If so... Then it bodes very ill...
